title: Add Strings
summary: Given two non-negative integers as strings, compute their sum and return the result as a string without using built-in large integer libraries or direct integer conversion.
statement: Given two non-negative integers as strings, compute their sum and return the result as a string without using built-in large integer libraries or direct integer conversion.
constraints: 1 <= each input length <= 10,000; decimal digits only.
No leading zeros except the string "0". Return the exact decimal sum as a string.
Do not convert a whole input to an integer or use a large-integer library; operate on digits.
reference_solution:
def add_decimal_strings(num1, num2):
    i,j,carry = len(num1)-1,len(num2)-1,0
    digits = []
    while i>=0 or j>=0 or carry:
        a = ord(num1[i])-ord('0') if i>=0 else 0
        b = ord(num2[j])-ord('0') if j>=0 else 0
        total = a+b+carry
        digits.append(chr(ord('0')+total%10))
        carry = total//10
        i,j = i-1,j-1
    return ''.join(reversed(digits))

hints: Decimal addition needs only one digit from each input and a carry.
Traverse right to left, treating exhausted inputs as zero.
Append total%10 and retain total//10 while either input or carry remains; reverse the collected digits.
Processing each position once gives linear time. The output may have one more digit than either input.
editorial: Use character codes to read a single digit. Add both digits and the previous carry, emit the ones place, and carry the tens place. Missing high digits act as zero. The final carry needs its own iteration. Reverse the collected characters once; repeated front insertion would be quadratic.
